Paragraph:
Translation: The wise, engaged in devotional service, take refuge in the Lord, and free themselves from the cycle of birth and death by renouncing the fruits of action in the material world. In this way they can attain that state beyond all miseries.

Purport (Excerpt): ...Owing to ignorance, one does not know that this material world is a miserable place where there are dangers at every step. Out of ignorance only, less intelligent persons try to adjust to the situation by fruitive activities, thinking that resultant actions will make them happy. They do not know that no kind of material body anywhere within the universe can give life without miseries...
Situation/Problem_Faced: Humans constantly try to "adjust" to their suffering by rearranging their material circumstances (e.g., getting a new job, buying a new house), mistakenly believing these external changes will bring permanent relief.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna introduces a radical perspective: the material world is inherently a place of misery (dangers at every step). True wisdom lies not in trying to make a miserable place perfectly comfortable, but in breaking the cycle entirely by renouncing outcome-driven (fruitive) action and seeking refuge in the Divine.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna is pointed toward 'Param padam' (the state beyond all miseries), shifting his focus from temporary material fixes to eternal spiritual liberation.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Radical Acceptance: Acknowledging that pain and danger are inherent to physical existence
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.The Futility of External Fixes: Realizing that trying to "adjust" material situations will never yield permanent happiness
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Existential Suffering: The core miseries (birth, death, old age, disease) that no amount of success can prevent

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Mukti/Moksha (Liberation from the cycle of birth and death)
Vaikuntha (The spiritual realm devoid of anxiety and misery)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The material world is structurally designed to contain suffering (birth, disease, old age, death). Foolish people try to manipulate this world through fruitive karma to extract permanent happiness. The wise recognize this design flaw, detach from the results of their actions, and take shelter of the Supreme Lord to achieve total liberation.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This verse aligns closely with the psychological concept of 'Radical Acceptance.' Anxiety often stems from our relentless, exhausting attempts to control and sanitize our environment to avoid pain. Krishna advises accepting that life fundamentally involves discomfort ('dangers at every step'). By stopping the desperate attempt to 'adjust the situation' for perfect material happiness, we actually find a profound psychological relief.
